about: Which vault paths are the knowledge/ bundle, and the one spelling each is filed under (M49.4, M53.28). Judged on the path the filesystem resolves, not the raw string: empty and `.` segments drop, `..` pops, and a path that climbs out of the vault, or starts with `/`, is not in the bundle. The first name is heard as a folding disk hears it: with the code points HFS+ ignores dropped, and Unicode case folded (to upper case, then to lower), it is `knowledge`. Only that name is respelled; the rest of the path stays as asked. A sibling that only shares the prefix is not the bundle. Replayed through canonical_path and is_knowledge_path by recognizes_the_bundle_but_not_a_lookalike_sibling in src-tauri/src/knowledge.rs, and through canonicalKnowledgePath and isKnowledgePath by src/engine/okf.test.ts. `canonical` is the bundle path in its one spelling, or null when the path is not in the bundle; `why` is for the reader.

cases.why: APFS folds case, so on the disk the app ships for this IS knowledge/.
APFS folds Unicode case, not only ASCII: it hears U+212A KELVIN SIGN as k.
HFS+ ignores U+200C ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER in a name (git's core.protectHFS class).
HFS+ ignores U+FEFF, the byte order mark, in a name too.
Only the bundle's own name is respelled.
It climbs out of the vault.
A sibling that shares the prefix is not the bundle.
Folded, it is still the sibling.
